name: composer
title: Composer
description: A chat's message box: text with chips in it for mentions, files (an image's thumbnail, an upload's progress or why it failed) and links, at the caret where they came in, or files in a row above it: images as 64px tiles in a sideways-scrolling line (a progress ring or warning over the image, remove/retry on the corner on hover or focus, always on touch or error), other files as 44px cards (a 32px icon or upload ring, the name over its state, a round × always on the corner, a failed one's edge dashed), or as the text's chips; a pasted address becomes a titled link once the app resolves it, with a bar to keep it as a link, a preview or plain text; a chip is selected by Backspace or the arrows and shows a card to open, retry or remove it; mentions suggested as you type a trigger such as @ or #, the list under the trigger, the send button grey while it is open (Enter takes a suggestion); Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line (not while an input method composes, nor on touch screens); inside a ``` code block Enter adds a line keeping the indent and never sends, Enter at the closing fence or after two blank lines leaves the block, Tab and Shift+Tab indent and outdent the lines, pastes stay typed text and mentions are not suggested; one button sends or stops the running response without losing focus, and while a turn runs says what sending does (followUp: send, queue or steer) by its icon and name, with a tooltip naming the Cmd/Ctrl-click alternative; past eight lines it scrolls and expands (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E) to a page of writing with a word count, its Markdown styled as typed (marks kept and muted, headings semibold, code in mono; the text unchanged), and a Markdown preview (ComposerEditor's previewProps: Markdown's labels, headingOffset and other props); files come in by an attach button, pasting or dropping, and long pasted text can come in as a file. Its box has the theme's rounded-composer corner and a shadow for its edge (no border, so no focus outline: the caret shows focus; a border in forced colors); the toolbar's menus open 8px above it, not over the text (popups="trigger": by their buttons instead). Where its toolbar is narrower than 36rem (a phone, or beside a sidebar on an unfolded foldable), or where unfolded its tools do not fit (a picker's value cut short), a step at a time (a compact ComposerOptionsFold to its icon and the rest, its value gone, in place first; those not keep away next), ComposerOptions folds the tools in ComposerOptionsFold (permissions, the context meter) behind one button and a sheet of ComposerOptionsItem rows; a folded picker opened from a row opens from that button. ComposerTakeover puts what the agent waits for (an agent-request: an approval, a question) in the composer's place and frame, one at a time, under a line of the app's status and a stop, a question settable aside to chat; the composer stays mounted, hidden and inert, its draft kept, and focus moves to the request and back to the editor. A request arriving while the reader types is held until they pause (holdWhileTyping, 1.5s by default), or at once on blur or send; the composer keeps focus and keystrokes, with a quiet hint announced politely. ComposerMessage shows a sent message's chips the same way. ComposerShelf sits over the composer tucked under its top edge, a little narrower; several stack edge to edge, square where they meet with one hairline, fading in; ComposerShelfTab is a small content-width tab at the top-right edge whose count lifts once when it rises (not with reduced motion); the app renders shelves in a fixed order so rows never swap. ComposerVoice dictates: tapped it records until Done, held (pointer or Space) until let go, slid back to cancel; its words go where the caret was as it started (over a selection; else at the end), a space between them and the draft where the script needs one (none beside Chinese or Japanese: dictationSpaces in lib/dictation); while it records the editor is read only, the draft in view as it will be, the time and a waveform above it, or a live transcript (transcript, its interim words grey) in the draft where it goes, the time on the toolbar; why it would not start under the box, by getUserMedia's error names (access off, no microphone); a take whose words could not be made out kept, with Retry; maxDuration counting its last 10 seconds down; submitOnFinish sending at once (always, or when held). A shortcut (a KeyboardEvent.code, e.g. AltRight) drives it from anywhere in the window, pressed alone: held, it records until let go (Escape cancels); tapped, until tapped again; another key with it (an Option or AltGr character) starts none or cancels it and goes through; the window left while held finishes it, unsent; of several composers, the one with the focus answers, else the one that last had it; labels.shortcut in the mic's tooltip and description, naming the key exactly (by default from its code, "Hold Right Alt to talk"), as aria-keyshortcuts ("Alt") cannot. While onStart is pending, a spinner in the mic's glyph's place (still with reduced motion), the mic busy and described as starting; ready (the app keeps the microphone open, a press records at once) shows on the idle mic as its glyph in the text's colour and a dot at its corner, described as Microphone ready. holdToTalk, on a touch screen: a tap on the composer types, a long press (400ms, before the platform's) talks: with the keyboard down anywhere on the composer, the editor too (its selection and callout held off for that press), with the editor focused only off its text; held, its words, time and waveform over the conversation, what letting go does, and Cancel and To text targets for the finger (lit, saying what letting go there does, a short vibration); let go elsewhere, its words are sent alone, the draft kept (onSubmit's options.talk), on To text they go in at the caret, the editor focused; a finger moved first is a scroll, a second finger or a cancelled touch drops it, the page hidden puts it in the text. However a take ends, the editor has the focus again, the caret after its words or where it was (the focus fell to the page, where typing went nowhere; in WebKit the caret went to the start). Given inputs, a chevron beside the mic (a split button; tap, hold and Space stay the mic's) opens a choice of what to record from, the system default first, a sheet on a phone, not while recording or starting; the app lists the devices (onInputsOpen to list them again), keeps the choice (input, onInputChange) and records from it. Built on Lexical, which apps do not see. A quote (e.g. from selection-actions) is a chip of its first words, its card its source and whole text with Open (onOpenQuote, also Enter) and Remove; copied as a Markdown quote.
